extracted.intended_audience: attorneys admitted to practice and authorized to practice before the USPTO (especially those facing or administering reciprocal discipline), USPTO/OED staff, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under USPTO regulations (37 C.F.R. § 11.24), describing the grounds, procedural steps, publication/notice requirements, and duties arising from suspension of an attorney's non-patent practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided the Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If the Notice cannot be delivered, it may be published in the Official Gazette. Failure to respond can support a finding that there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) referenced as predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was suspended for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended for eighteen months from the practice of law by a State authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the USPTO action is ‘predicated upon being suspended… by a duly constituted authority of a State’ and cites § 11.804(h) as the rule violated; the state suspension’s findings supply the predicate misconduct for the USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings — Texas RPC 1.01(b)(1) (neglect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Texas Rules of Professional Conduct 1.01(b)(1) (neglect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of the neglect alleged include failing to file suit on behalf of a client within the applicable statute of limitations in a personal injury matter. The Order uses the state disciplinary findings as the basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings — Texas RPC 1.01(b)(2) (failure of diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Texas Rules of Professional Conduct 1.01(b)(2) (failure of diligence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites failing to carry out completely obligations owed to the client as an example supporting the failure-of-diligence determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings — Texas RPC 1.03(a) (failure to keep client informed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Texas Rule of Professional Conduct 1.03(a) (failure to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and failure to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter and failing to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client as factual bases for the rule violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings — Texas RPC 1.15(d) (failure to protect client's interests upon termination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Texas Rule of Professional Conduct 1.15(d) (failure to take reasonably practicable steps to protect a client's interests upon termination of representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references the state finding that the respondent failed to take reasonably practicable steps to protect the client's interests upon termination; the USPTO relies on that state determination when imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline (suspension period and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO imposed suspension from the practice of trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO for eighteen (18) months — identical to the state-imposed discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states Respondent is suspended from trademark and other non-patent matters for eighteen months, reflecting the reciprocal discipline principle of imposing identical discipline unless a statutory exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of suspension (non-patent/trademark practice vs. patent practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension applies to practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters; Respondent is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice language clarifies scope: ‘Mr. Wiltz is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters.’ USPTO reciprocal discipline can be limited to non-patent practice when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural finding on failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response to the Notice and Order, it is determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and reciprocal suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains that a respondent’s failure to timely oppose the Notice and Order supports entering reciprocal discipline without creating a material factual dispute; this reflects § 11.24(d) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and official notice requirements (FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided model text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes model Official Gazette language to be used and requires electronic publication in the FOIA Reading Room (link provided). If initial notice cannot be delivered, publication in the Official Gazette is an alternative mechanism for notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision requires dissemination of the discipline beyond USPTO publication to relevant state agencies and courts, ensuring cross-jurisdictional notice of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of suspended practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 upon suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs compliance with § 11.58 (duties upon suspension/discipline) but does not reproduce the duties; practitioners must consult § 11.58 for obligations such as notification and restrictions during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be served (mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested) to the Respondent at addresses listed when filing and to addresses where OED reasonably believes Respondent receives mail, and via email to the Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a Certificate of Service showing mailing to multiple addresses, and electronic service via email; it demonstrates the procedural requirement to attempt multiple means of service and to document service for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary actions; practitioners and adjudicators should rely on these provisions when assessing jurisdiction and procedural bases for reciprocal discipline.
